subject: Discrepancy: Marketplace settlements, currency FX and withholding on Mar invoices
messages:
From: NorthStar Finance <finance@northstaranalytics.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Mar 2029 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Discrepancy in Mar marketplace settlements (AWS + GCP)

Hi Rachel,

We're reconciling March marketplace payouts and spotting two issues that don't match our ledger:

1) AWS settlement shows a negative adjustment that was recorded in USD, but our contract states EUR billing for our EU entity — the FX applied doesn't match the exchange used in the invoice.
2) GCP payout appears to have a withholding tax line (1.5%) applied to the payout; there wasn't a prior memo about withholding at signup.

Attached is our quick CSV with the rows we flagged (NorthStar_Mar2029_invoice_summary.csv). Can you confirm what's driving these adjustments and whether Redwood is seeing corresponding gross-to-net mismatches? We need to get this clarified before our month-end close.

Thanks,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Finance — NorthStar Analytics
finance@northstaranalytics.com

(Attachment: NorthStar_Mar2029_invoice_summary.csv)

Hi Marta — thanks for the clear breakdown and the CSV. I'm looping in Vanessa and Markus from our billing and marketplace ops teams to dig into both the FX and withholding questions.

High-level next steps:
- Vanessa will pull the AWS settlement report for your account and confirm whether Redwood routed the payout through our EU billing entity or an alternate marketplace entity. That explains the FX direction.
- Markus will validate the GCP payout file to see if withholding was applied by the marketplace partner vs. an upstream tax withholding performed by our payout processor.

Can you confirm the preferred billing entity on your side (NorthStar EU vs NorthStar Global) for March? That will speed routing checks.

I'll follow up with a consolidated note and any exportable settlement artifacts.

Best,
Rachel Kim

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Mar 2029 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in Mar marketplace settlements (AWS + GCP)

Hi all — I pulled the AWS settlement for NorthStar (listing: northstar-analytics-prod) and here's what I see:

- AWS issued two settlement files for March: the regular monthly settlement (invoice currency EUR) and a post-month correction (USD) that related to an earlier SKU reclassification.
- Our payment orchestration routed the EUR settlement through Redwood EU (entity ID: RW-EU-03). The correction was processed through our US clearing account which caused the USD net to appear on a separate payout run.
- FX used: the USD correction was converted to EUR at a bank rate recorded on 2029-03-02 (we store the conversion rate in settlement metadata), but NorthStar's ledger shows a different FX (your team appears to be using a same-day market close rate).

Action items I propose:
- We can re-run the USD correction through the EU entity and issue a consolidated correction payout in EUR — this requires a manual settlement reallocation and will be processed in the next payout window (two-week lead).
- Alternatively, we can provide a detailed reconciliation file showing the USD-to-EUR conversion and the clearing account routing for your GL team to apply your own FX adjustments.

I've attached our AWS settlement export and flagged the relevant rows in aws-settlement-202903.pdf.

Vanessa
Marketplace Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: aws-settlement-202903.pdf)

Thanks Vanessa — quick note on the GCP side after checking the payout CSV:

- GCP appears to have applied a 1.5% withholding labeled as "local tax withholding" on the gross payout to the US clearing account. That withholding is applied before Redwood takes our fee, so the net posted to our clearing account is lower.
- Our contract with GCP marketplace requires us to pass through any partner-levied withholdings, but we should have communicated that for EU customers flagged for local tax nexus. Looks like the notification step didn't include NorthStar.

Options to resolve:
1) Issue a one-time credit to NorthStar equal to the withheld amount (gross-up) and absorb cost on Redwood — we should only do this with leadership approval for material amounts.
2) Re-route future payouts for NorthStar through an entity in the jurisdiction that avoids partner withholding (if available).
3) Provide NorthStar with a detailed withholding proof bundle so they can claim the credit or VAT reclaim on their side.

I'll prepare the withholding proof (payout CSV + partner withhold memo) and share it in the next message.

-Markus
Finance, Redwood Inference
